messages:
arthur: Quick report from an onboarding session — the repo's setup script and .env.example disagree with our canonical names and a few SDK snippets are out of sync. New hires hit 3 separate blockers in one hour.

rachel: ugh. which repo/sample is this?

arthur: the `hello-world` quickstart. two problems: 1) `scripts/setup.sh` auto-writes a .env with AUTH_TOKEN and REDWOOD_KEY, 2) the Windows installer doc references api.redwood-inference.com (old host). also the Rust and C# snippets use different env names.

mina: can you paste the offending lines?

arthur: sure. current .env.example generated by setup.sh:```env
# .env.example (wrong)
AUTH_TOKEN=sk_test_xxx
REDWOOD_KEY=sk_test_yyy
API_HOST=https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1
```and Rust snippet in README:```rust
// wrong (README)
let client = Client::new(std::env::var("REDWOOD_TOKEN").unwrap());
```C# sample:```csharp
// wrong (README)
var client = new RedwoodClient(apiKey: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AUTH_TOKEN"));
```

rachel: yikes. that's a lot of drift. canonical is REDWOOD_API_KEY and host is https://api.redwood.ai/v1.

arthur: exactly. proposed fixes I pushed in a local branch: change setup.sh to write .env.example with REDWOOD_API_KEY and API_HOST https://api.redwood.ai/v1, update Rust to show both env auto-detect and explicit constructor, and same for C#. Also add PowerShell example for Windows. Suggested corrected snippets:
```env
# .env.example (fixed)
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_...
API_HOST=https://api.redwood.ai/v1
```Rust:
```rust
// recommended: env auto-detect
let client = Client::default(); // reads REDWOOD_API_KEY
// or explicit
let client = Client::with_api_key(std::env::var("REDWOOD_API_KEY").unwrap());
```C#:
```csharp
// env auto-detect
var client = new RedwoodClient(); // reads REDWOOD_API_KEY
// or explicit
var client = new RedwoodClient(apiKey: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("REDWOOD_API_KEY"));
```PowerShell note:
```powershell
# PowerShell (session)
$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk_live_...'
# one-off flag example (CLI supports --api-key)
redwood generate --model redwood-v1 --prompt "hello" --api-key $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY
```

kevin: nice. also callout that setup.sh previously encouraged writing tokens into .env committed to repo. please replace with a .env.local template and document `docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY` or `export` in CI. we should also add a short security note: never commit secrets.

sam: small parity item: retry defaults differ across SDKs and this quickstart references "retries enabled" but never lists counts. we get questions: Node=5, Python=3, Rust=4 (recent change). the quickstart should have a tiny table and link to retry config.

mina: agree. can you include a brief snippet showing how to override retries in each SDK? e.g., Rust: `Client::builder().max_retries(2).build()` etc.

arthur: will add those. I'll also add a CI lint in the sample that runs a tiny regex to ensure README env names match .env.example to prevent this drift.

rachel: docs-bot, please open an issue for this triage (env drift + host + Rust/C# parity + retry docs + security note).

docs-bot: opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1024 - "hello-world quickstart: .env/setup.sh writes wrong names, old host, Rust/C# snippets, retry defaults & security note" assigned to @arthur and @mina

sam: i'll review the Rust retry snippet and confirm exact default backoff params.

kevin: i'll review the C# and Windows/installer docs. if you can, include a note about PowerShell quoting (use single quotes for literals) and an explicit example showing escaping for double quotes.

mina: i'll open the PR to update setup.sh, .env.example, README snippets, and add the troubleshooting box "If you see 401": list top causes (wrong env var, missing Bearer header, old host). will also add the CI lint. PR in ~45m.

arthur: thanks all. these are tiny fixes but block a lot of first-run users.

rachel: appreciated. tagging @kevin and @sam for SDK checks once PR is up. :sparkles:
